metadata.scenario_context: Jeff, Anne, and Sarah are colleagues at a tech startup and have decided to cook together to celebrate some recent achievements they have made within the company. They intend to discuss the recent news reports about AI advancements that could potentially benefit their business.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Peru have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_1: Choosing and discussing the menu for their cooking session.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Jeff, have you ever thought about trying to make a salted dessert? I think it could be a fun twist for our cooking session. 

Also, I've been wondering... do you think people really have confidence in the press these days?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jeff
shared_prefix.message: A salted dessert sounds interesting... maybe we could try something like salted caramel? But about the press... I really don't think many people trust it. In Peru, we’ve seen so many biased reports. I mean... it's hard to believe what you read.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sarah
shared_prefix.message: Actually, that's not how it works, Jeff. In Canada, we have a great deal of confidence in the press. Properly speaking, most people trust the information they receive. It’s just a different standard. I think it's a bit naive to dismiss the press completely based on biased reports you've seen. In our way, we value accurate reporting. It’s essential for an informed society.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Jeff
